chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"There is no harm in freeing the child of fornication."

key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on freeing a slave who is the child of a fornicator?
ai.summary: Reported by Shaykh al-Tusi in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith clarifies that the offspring of a fornicator (walad al-zina) are not inherently disqualified from manumission, affirming their legal capacity as slaves who can be freed. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that the specific sin of the parent does not permanently taint the child’s status regarding emancipation, distinguishing it from other legal impediments. It highlights the principle of individual accountability and the ease with which such slaves may be elevated to freedom.
